44398-poems-on-slavery.title: Slavery.
44398-poems-on-slavery.creator: Unknown
44398-poems-on-slavery.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The pages of thy book I read, And as I closed each one, My heart, responding, ever said, "Servant of God! well done!" Well done! Thy words are great and bold; At times they seem to me, Like Luther's, in the days of old, Half-battles for the free. Go on, until this land revokes The old and chartered Lie, The feudal curse, whose whips and yokes Insult humanity.

Somehow or another Dick looked to unusual advantage in knickerbockers, and he made a pretty figure in the store, which naturally made his employer partial to that kind of attire in him.

arxiv-1802-06012.title: WebEye– Automated Collection of Malicious HTTP Traffic
arxiv-1802-06012.creator: Johann Vierthaler, Roman Kruszelnicki, Julian Schütte
arxiv-1802-06012.description: Abstract With malware detection techniques increasingly adopting machine learning approaches, the creation of precise training sets becomes more and more important. Large data sets of realistic web traffic, correctly classified as benign or malicious are needed, not only to train classic and deep learning algorithms, but also to serve as evaluation benchmarks for existing malware detection products.

arxiv-2104-00243.title: Hydrogel sphere impact cratering, spreading and bouncing on granular media
arxiv-2104-00243.creator: Xiaoyan Ye 1 and Devaraj van der Meer 2
arxiv-2104-00243.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xiaoyan Ye 1 and Devaraj van der Meer 2. The impact of a hydrogel sphere onto a granular target results in both the deformation of the sphere and the formation of a prominent topographic feature known as impact crater on the granular surface.

arxiv-2111-05905.title: Model independent search for transient multimessenger events with AMON using outlier detection methods
arxiv-2111-05905.creator: for the AMON group
arxiv-2111-05905.description: Abstract The Astrophysical Multimessenger Observatory Network (AMON) receives subthreshold data from multiple observatories in order to look for coincidences. Combining more than two datasets at the same time is challenging because of the range of possible signals (time windows, energies, number of events…). arxiv-2206-13426.title: Thermal spin current generation in the multifunctional ferrimagnet Ga 0.6 Fe 1.4 O 3

arxiv-2207-07156.title: Enhanced power graphs of groups are weakly perfect
arxiv-2207-07156.creator: Peter J. Cameron, Veronica Phan
arxiv-2207-07156.description: Abstract A graph is weakly perfect if its clique number and chromatic number are equal. We show that the enhanced power graph of a finite group G G is weakly perfect: its clique number and chromatic number are equal to the maximum order of an element of G G . The proof requires a combinatorial lemma.

arxiv-2305-19776.title: Off-By-One Implementation Error in J-UNIWARD
arxiv-2305-19776.creator: Benedikt Lorch Security and Privacy Lab Universität Innsbruck
arxiv-2305-19776.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Benedikt Lorch Security and Privacy Lab Universität Innsbruck. J-UNIWARD is a popular steganography method for hiding secret messages in JPEG cover images. As a content-adaptive method, J-UNIWARD aims to embed into textured image regions where changes are difficult to detect. To this end, J-UNIWARD first assigns to each DCT coefficient an embedding cost calculated based on the image’s Wavelet residual, and then uses a coding method that minimizes the cost while embedding the desired payload.

arxiv-2409-02191.title: Z ′ Z^{\prime} -mediated dark matter freeze-in at stronger coupling
arxiv-2409-02191.creator: Oleg Lebedev
arxiv-2409-02191.description: Abstract We study freeze-in production of fermionic dark matter mediated by a Z ′ Z^{\prime} gauge boson. In particular, we explore the regime of Boltzmann-suppressed production, when the Standard Model (SM) thermal bath temperature never exceeds the dark matter mass. The corresponding gauge coupling is then required to be significant, up to order one.

arxiv-2503-07313.title: The influence of missing data mechanisms and simple missing data handling techniques on fairness
arxiv-2503-07313.creator: Aeysha Bhatti, Trudie Sandrock, Johané Nienkemper-Swanepoel
arxiv-2503-07313.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aeysha Bhatti, Trudie Sandrock, Johané Nienkemper-Swanepoel. Machine learning algorithms permeate the day-to-day aspects of our lives and therefore studying the fairness of these algorithms before implementation is crucial. One way in which bias can manifest in a dataset is through missing values. Missing data are often assumed to be missing completely randomly; in reality the propensity of data being missing is often tied to the demographic characteristics of individuals.

arxiv-2505-13116.title: Continuous Fair SMOTE – Fairness-Aware Stream Learning from Imbalanced Data
arxiv-2505-13116.creator: Kathrin Lammers, Valerie Vaquet, Barbara Hammer
arxiv-2505-13116.description: Abstract As machine learning is increasingly applied in an online fashion to deal with evolving data streams, the fairness of these algorithms is a matter of growing ethical and legal concern. In many use cases, class imbalance in the data also needs to be dealt with to ensure predictive performance.

arxiv-2602-22471.title: Faculty of Fundamental Science,
arxiv-2602-22471.creator: National Institute of Technology (KOSEN), Niihama College,
arxiv-2602-22471.description: Abstract Analogue of the theta group \Gamma_{\theta} By Kazuhide Matsuda Abstract In this paper, we introduce higher level versions of the theta group \Gamma_{\theta}. In particular, we treat level 3 and 4 versions of the theta group, \Gamma_{\theta,3} and \Gamma_{\theta,4} and prove that \displaystyle F(\tau)=\eta\left(\frac{\tau-1}{3}\right)\eta\left(\frac{\tau+1}{3}\right) and \displaystyle G(\tau)=\eta\left(\frac{\tau-1}{4}\right)\eta\left(\frac{\tau+1}{4}\right) are modular forms on \Gamma_{\theta,3} and \Gamma_{\theta,4} respectively.

pmc-11358971.title: New Insights into the Connections between Flooding/Hypoxia Response and Plant Defenses against Pathogens
pmc-11358971.creator: Pablo García, Shreenivas Singh, Emmanuelle Graciet
pmc-11358971.description: The impact of global climate change has highlighted the need for a better understanding of how plants respond to multiple simultaneous or sequential stresses, not only to gain fundamental knowledge of how plants integrate signals and mount a coordinated response to stresses but also for applications to improve crop resilience to environmental stresses.

pmc-11428890.title: Increasing Fluroquinolone Susceptibility and Genetic Diversity of ESBL-Producing E. coli from the Lower Respiratory Tract during the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-11428890.creator: Katja Hrovat, Katja Seme, Jerneja Ambrožič Avguštin, Shailendra K Saxena, Swatantra Kumar
pmc-11428890.description: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) are the fourth leading cause of death worldwide, among which Escherichia coli (E. coli) pneumonia is considered a rare phenomenon. Treatment options for LRTIs have become limited, especially for extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing E. coli (ESBL-EC), which are usually resistant to other groups of antimicrobials as well.

pmc-11642526.title: Recent Advances in the Management of Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis
pmc-11642526.creator: Elaine Ong Ming San, Kassem Sharif, Konstantina Rosiou, Michael Rennie, Christian Philipp Selinger, Peter Laszlo Lakatos
pmc-11642526.description: Acute severe ulcerative colitis is a medical emergency requiring inpatient treatment with intravenous steroids. Approximately one-third of patients do not respond to steroids sufficiently and require medical rescue therapy. Infliximab and cyclosporine are equally effective rescue agents, though infliximab is often preferred by clinicians for ease of use and greater familiarity.

pmc-12554497.title: The mechanism and research progress of PD-1/PD-L1 on immune escape of lung cancer
pmc-12554497.creator: Zhenyu Li, Tan Wang, Jimin Liu, Wenlong Qi, Qingguo Lv, Yannan Xu, Lin Tian
pmc-12554497.description: According to the latest Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2022 estimates, lung cancer remains the second most commonly diagnosed cancer worldwide, with approximately 2.48 million new cases (11.4% of all cancer diagnoses) and over 1.86 million deaths (18.2% of all cancer-related deaths), making it the leading cause of cancer mortality globally.

pmc-12556998.title: Assessing Planetary Health training needs in Italy: a survey of institutions perspectives
pmc-12556998.creator: T Scirocco, F Panariello, S Mao, W Ricciardi, L Villani
pmc-12556998.description: BackgroundThe Planetary Health approach, which explores the links between human health and the disruption of ecological systems, is increasingly recognized as crucial for addressing the health challenges of the 21st century. Effective educational training is essential to build a competent workforce, especially in countries like Italy, which faces significant environmental pressures.

pmc-12837123.title: Barriers and facilitators in preventing and managing parastomal hernias: a qualitative study from the perspective of enterostomal therapist
pmc-12837123.creator: Xinyan Che, Yisen Meng, Dong Pang, Han Song, Jianing Han, Jianfeng Zhang, Shuhui Yu
pmc-12837123.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundA parastomal hernia is a common complication of ostomies. Once developed, it is typically irreversible and can significantly impair a patient’s quality of life. Despite their prevalence, current strategies for the prevention and management of parastomal hernias remain inadequate. Previous research has explored the influencing factors from the patient’s perspective; however, there is a notable lack of in-depth analysis from the viewpoint of Enterostomal Therapists.

pmc-13058240.title: Tracking Inter‐ and Intraspecific Bacterial Competition in Pairwise Assays Using a Transient Fluorescent Dye
pmc-13058240.creator: Julius Hoffmann, Ole Johannsen, Lutz Becks
pmc-13058240.description: Testing inter‐ and intraspecific competition is essential for understanding the processes that maintain diversity within communities and populations. Pairwise growth assays are well‐established methods to study the outcome of competition between bacterial genotypes or species. However, distinguishing bacterial competitors in coculture remains a major challenge due to their small cell size, similar cell morphology, and often large population sizes.

pmc-13087073.title: Multifunctional effects of Zizyphus mauritiana leaf extract on oral pathogens and wound healing: an integrative in vitro and in vivo study
pmc-13087073.creator: Wiwiek Poedjiastoeti, Rachendra Pratama, Irvan Septrian Syah Putra Rasad, Indrayadi Gunardi, Jonathan Agung Suryowinahyu, Felicia Klarissa Tanzil, Armelia Sari Widyarman, Chaminda Jayampath Seneviratne
pmc-13087073.description: Post-extraction infections and delayed oral wound healing remain clinical challenges due to bacterial biofilms, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Natural plant-derived compounds offer promising alternatives to conventional antimicrobials. Zizyphus mauritiana (daun bidara), widely used in traditional Indonesian medicine, has not been comprehensively evaluated for its potential role in oral infection control and wound repair.

pmc-13389171.title: Structural basis of chondroitin sulfate backbone polymer synthesis
pmc-13389171.creator: Daniel Tehrani, Nil Cortiella-Valls, Chin Huang, Digantkumar Chapla, Zhifeng Zheng, Aarya Venkat, Brady O’Boyle, Natarajan Kannan, Camilo Perez, Kelley W. Moremen
pmc-13389171.description: Chondroitin sulfate (CS) proteoglycans are extended (-GlcAβ1,3GalNAcβ1,4-)n co-polymers attached to cell surface and extracellular matrix core proteins that are further modified by extensive sulfation and epimerization. Four homologous proteins contribute to CS backbone synthesis (CHPF1, CHPF2, CHSY1, and CHSY3) and prior data suggests assembly of the proteins into heterocomplexes is required for function.

pmc-13472468.title: Evaluating the therapeutic potential of Salacca zalacca peel ethanol extract on probing depth and gingival recession in Wistar rats with periodontitis

pmc-13496237.title: Preliminary evaluation of beta-endorphin alone and in combination with adrenocorticotropic hormone for the diagnosis of pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction in equids
pmc-13496237.creator: Paula Billmann, Andy E Durham, Garance Christen, Vinzenz Gerber, Josef Gross, Nathalie Fouché
pmc-13496237.description: BackgroundLimited published data exist regarding the diagnostic utility of beta-endorphin (β-END) for pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID), either compared with or in combination with adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH).Hypothesis/ObjectivesTo evaluate β-END as a potential diagnostic test for PPID in comparison with ACTH and to explore the diagnostic performance of combined tests.

pmc-13689778.title: Thoracic Duct Obstruction as a Cause of Chylous Ascites After Pacemaker Implant
pmc-13689778.creator: Banveet Kaur, Maxim Itkin, Robert D. Schaller
pmc-13689778.description: BackgroundTransvenous leads of cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) can cause central venous stenosis, impairing thoracic duct outflow, and result in chylous effusions.Case SummaryA 48-year-old man developed refractory chylous ascites/chylothorax after pacemaker implantation. Magnetic resonance lymphangiography demonstrated thoracic duct dilatation and mesenteric reflux secondary to venous stenosis. Thoracic duct thrombolysis provided only temporary improvement.
